reference: GNU coreutils tac selected from PATH under system Bash; the runner checks its expected status first, then compares raw stdout and the fixture tree. Contract metadata assertions use Bash's type/help builtins and the documented tac synopsis/help text.
coverage: Default newline records from stdin, including empty input, adjacent blank records, and a missing final newline.
Custom literal separators, multiple files in operand order, and trailing separators.
-b separator attachment with leading and adjacent multi-byte separators.
An empty -s argument selecting NUL record boundaries on pipe input.
GNU Emacs regex character-class repetition and dot behavior across NUL/newline bytes.
GNU option permutation after an operand and -- handling for a dash-leading relative fixture path.
Missing-file continuation and invalid-option exit/error behavior.
Bash builtin availability and documented help metadata.
exclusions: PTY-specific shell stdout ordering and flush behavior is deferred because the runner has no terminal driver.
No /dev paths, output-device failures, locale matrix, large-input stress, concurrent file mutation, or system operations are exercised.
Advanced GNU regex anchor corner cases and resource-limit behavior are outside this compact suite.

cases.purpose: Check default newline records on stdin, including empty input, blank records, and an unterminated last record.
cases.script:
: > empty
tac < empty
printf '%s\n' '---'
printf 'A\n\nB' | tac

cases.purpose: Check GNU literal multi-byte separator handling across two files, preserving operand order and a trailing separator.
cases.script:
printf '%s' 'one::two::tail' > first
printf '%s' 'red::blue::' > second
tac --separator='::' first second

cases.purpose: Check -b with a multi-byte separator at the start and between adjacent records.
Check that an empty -s argument selects NUL separators and preserves empty binary records from stdin.
Check GNU Emacs regex character-class repetition, whose reverse matching differs from ordinary forward splitting.
Check GNU regex dot matching NUL while excluding newline in a binary stdin stream.
Check options after an operand and -- protection for a dash-leading relative file name.
cases.script:
printf '%s' 'one::two::tail' > records
printf 'first\nsecond\n' > -dash
tac records --before --separator=::
tac -- -dash

cases.purpose: Check that a missing operand reports failure but tac still processes a following valid relative file.
Check nonzero status and a diagnostic for an unknown option without constraining GNU wording.
Check Bash reports tac as a builtin and exposes the documented synopsis and key help text through help tac.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t tac) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help_text=$(help tac)
[[ $help_text == *'tac [OPTION]... [FILE]...'* && $help_text == *'Concatenate and print files in reverse'* && $help_text == *'GNU Emacs regex'* ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' 'type/help metadata contract verified'

cases.purpose: Verify Bash output ordering and tac's flush behavior when builtin output shares a terminal stream.
cases.reason: The runner does not provide a PTY driver. A future isolated PTY fixture should write a Bash prefix, invoke builtin tac on controlled input, capture prefix/tac/suffix byte order and flush boundaries, then confirm the shell remains usable; use only a disposable local PTY, never a host terminal.

cases.purpose: Compare overlapping literal separators in both attachment modes and a separator longer than the input.
cases.script:
printf '%s' ababa | tac -s aba
printf '\n'
printf '%s' ababa | tac -b -s aba
printf '\n'
printf '%s' abc | tac -s abcdef

cases.purpose: Repeated calls in one shell must use the newly redirected input without stale EOF or buffered bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'a\nb\n' > one
printf 'c\nd' > two
tac < one
tac < two
